claims.evidence: Each of the 12 deposited design basenames matches one distinct acquisition directory in the RAW ZIP central directory.
The design groups have 6_CTRL, 6_dTAG, 6A_CTRL and 6A_dTAG. The prefix is preserved without assigning genotype or interpreting A.
The design identifies CTRL and dTAG groups; PRIDE describes one-hour DMSO and dTAG treatment in the 12-sample experiment. CTRL to DMSO is a record-supported interpretation.

claims.value: 1-3 within each of four deposited groups
claims.evidence: The design has three distinct analytical samples per group and the paper states proteomics samples were triplicates prepared in parallel from cell seeding. Cross-condition pairing is not asserted.

claims.value: Homo sapiens; cell culture; Flp-In-T-REx-293; CVCL_U427
claims.evidence: PRIDE describes human INTS6 degron cells; the paper identifies the Flp-In T-REx HEK293 background; Cellosaurus verifies the base cell-line name and accession. The annotation does not assert a specific 6A derivative.

claims.location: comment[proteomics data acquisition method], [instrument], [cleavage agent details]
claims.evidence: All 12 run names contain DDA; PRIDE and paper describe timsTOF Pro PASEF and trypsin digestion in the MS protocol.
The sample protocol elutes in DTT and then chloroacetamide before overnight trypsin digestion.

limitations: The biological meaning of deposited cohort code 6A is not established. It may represent a genetic derivative, but no genotype is asserted and no 6-versus-6A biological contrast is encoded.
The PRIDE description says only the six 6_CTRL/6_dTAG runs appear in the publication; the remaining six are retained because they are deposited RAW acquisitions with explicit design groups.
Age, sex, disease, search mass tolerances, and modifications are not asserted because this accession's available evidence does not establish them.

The offline ontology cache does not resolve DMSO, dTAG, or the precise Cellosaurus cell-line name. The reconcile helper flags trypsin, although both PRIDE sample protocol and paper MS methods explicitly describe trypsin digestion.
